title: Cenote Knock Out, Akumal - Expéditions Yuc 95/96
credits: Cenote Knock Out (Akumal), plan and longitudinal section; topo J.A. Laclette, Edsel Rios, C. Thomas, Germano. Cenotes du Yucatan: Expéditions de 1995 et 1996, p. 65 (1996), reprinted in AMCS Activities Newsletter 35, p. 25 (2012)
sistemaWhy: Sistema created in the local database at the user's request (2026-10-02) from this map: Cenote Knock Out. No sistema or cave of the database is this cave: no name or aka contains Knock Out (nor Nocaut/Noqueo), and none of the database's Akumal caves matches it by name.
unverified: No position at all: Cenote Knock Out is in neither the database (names and akas), OpenStreetMap (Overpass name search over the Yucatán peninsula) nor a web search, and the map draws no road, coast, other cenote or coordinate - only the cave and a surface line with trees on the section. The single control point is a NOMINAL anchor (the entrance put on OpenStreetMap's Akumal village node, from the map's 'Akumal' caption), so the pipeline can run: the geometry is NOT on the ground (it lands across the Akumal access road). To fix: a field GPS of the entrance and the bearing of the cave's long axis (about 160 m from the -21 end to the -27 end).
placementWhy: UNVERIFIED (see 'unverified'). Same map as _data/cartes/à traiter/Knock Out, Cen., Akumal.pdf (Cenotes du Yucatan p. 65; AMCS Activities Newsletter 35 p. 25). Scale from the 0-30 m bar: x 1266-1700 at y 1155, 434 px = 30 m, 0.0691 m/px (its 10 m dividers at 1413 and 1555 agree within 3%); the plan, about 160 m end to end, matches the section drawn below it at the same scale. North from the 'Nord mg.' arrow pointing right (magnetic, 1996: a degree or two off true, not corrected): angle 90. Position nominal. The nearest placed map (murena) is about 200 m from the anchor; the map can't be cross-checked with any.

exclude.why: section (longitudinal profile, with trees on the surface)
credits: Topo J.A Laclette Edsel Rios C.Thomas.Germano
label Entrée (written on the dry chamber: the passage runs on under it)

controlPoints.name: NOMINAL anchor: the entrance (centre of the breakdown mound under the opening) put on OpenStreetMap's Akumal village node 854200484 - a namesake only, not a real position (see 'unverified')

entrances.name: Cenote Knock Out (Entrée)
entrances.why: The map's only opening to the surface, labelled Entrée: the ticked oval (drip line) over the breakdown mound, which the section shows under the entrance shaft. Not matched to a database cave: no cave or aka of the database is Knock Out.

prep.why: b/w hand drawing: the walls are bold closed outlines; dry parts left white, flooded parts hatched (the section shows water at both ends, air in the middle). fill_passages.py tints every enclosed interior pale blue for the colour-fill trace; the open passage ends are sealed by hand.

sealLines.why: gap in the east lobe's NE wall
open end of the east end's upper branch (narrow fissure, the Impenetrable end)

prep.passagePointsWhy: boulders (outlined blocks) on the breakdown mound under the entrance and in the east lobe: details, not pillars

trace.why: fill_passages.py tints the passages (see prep); colour-fill then traces the tint's outline as the walls, the two white pillars (the block in the east lobe, the sliver at the sand slope) as inner walls; hatching, stipple, boulders and slope/step lines kept as details. wallSimplifyMetres 0.15: a small map (0.069 m/px), the default 0.5 m cut the walls into straight segments.
trace.minHoleSqMetresWhy: the white sliver at the east sand slope (about 6.5 m2) is a pillar; the default 60 m2 dropped it
trace.waterWhy: mostly underwater: the hatching is water (the section shows air only in the entrance chamber, the passages dipping into water at both ends to -21 and -27); hatched passage is about 59% of the plan's area, plus all of its length beyond the entrance chamber. The white entrance chamber (breakdown mound under the opening, sand slopes stippled) is dry.

symbols.why: French expedition map (Yuc 95/96), same authors and style as jaguar-akumal: depths written with a minus sign (-21 at the end of the SW passage, -27 at the east end), Impenetrable at the east end, Entrée at the collapse. No legend, no letter codes. No flow arrows and no bones (checked by eye at full size; the small ticked marks in the hatched water are slope/step lines, the outlined blocks are boulders).

extra.label: Impenetrable
extra.why: label written below the east end's two branches, at the lower branch's end

fix.why: a boulder on the breakdown mound read as a circled 4
hatching tick read as a barred 4
